meta.tagline: From carbon accounting to carbon action.

deck.title: CarbonPilot
deck.lead: An AI carbon decision engine. It turns fragmented operational data into prioritised, financially-aware decarbonisation actions — and every number it prints is traceable to a calculation engine, never to the language model.
deck.foot: Working prototype · Gemini-driven agent over a deterministic engine · six screens, one loop
deck.notes: Open with the problem, not the product. The live URL is on the cover; if the venue network fails, this deck is the fallback.

deck.title: Companies can already measure their carbon. They still cannot decide what to do about it.

bullets.lead: The data exists, the decision does not.
bullets.text: Electricity, cloud, travel, fleet and procurement sit in CSVs and ERP exports. Aggregating them produces a number, not a plan.
A footprint tells you where you were. Management asks what changes next — and what it will cost.

bullets.lead: Carbon and money are decided separately.
bullets.text: The largest reduction is often the most expensive, and nobody can see the trade-off in one place.

deck.say: Knowing you emit eleven thousand tonnes does not tell you what to do next.
deck.foot: Demo company: 168 activity records, 12 months, across electricity, cloud, travel, fleet and procurement.
deck.notes: Name the persona: a sustainability or operations manager who has the data and keeps being asked ‘what do we do next?’ Do not say ‘all companies’.

deck.title: The same load is 3,036 tonnes here — and 399 in New Zealand. Location is a decision variable, not a footnote.

bullets.text: Twenty JAPAC grids from Ember Yearly Electricity Data (CC BY 4.0), one documented basis, labelled explicitly.

bullets.lead: Grid choice outweighs most single actions.
bullets.text: No reporting tool surfaces this — it sits in a footnote of the accounting exercise today.

deck.foot: Basis: full-lifecycle CO₂e intensity per kWh, Ember Yearly Electricity Data (CC BY 4.0). The product labels basis on every row; benchmark and inventory bases are never averaged together.
deck.notes: Land the JAPAC relevance: a regional benchmark is exactly what a JAPAC judge should expect — and the finding is real, not a demo artifact.

deck.title: It answers the question after the footprint.

steps.name: Ingest
steps.text: A CSV is mapped to canonical activity types and scopes. The interpretation is shown for confirmation before anything is written.

steps.name: Diagnose
steps.text: A robust median/MAD test finds the months that moved, then attributes each one to the activities that moved with it.

steps.name: Simulate
steps.text: Interventions are applied to the stored baseline; a constraint search explores combinations of them.

steps.name: Act
steps.text: Recommendations are ranked on carbon × cost × effort, weighted by factor confidence, and tracked to an owner.

deck.notes: Walk the loop once, top to bottom. Each stage is its own engine and its own screen — six screens in total.

deck.title: The language model never produces a carbon number.
deck.left_lead: The engine computes. The agent explains.
deck.left: Every kilogram of CO₂ is computed by a deterministic, unit-tested engine in app/engine/. The model chooses which analyses to run and explains the result — so its failure mode is “I could not find that”, never “here is a plausible number”.
deck.right: the quantity, the factor, the factor’s source and year, and the uncertainty. A judge can ask why a factor is defensible and get a cited answer, not a recollection.
deck.notes: This is the answer to ‘is this just an LLM wrapper?’. Land it before showing any number.

deck.title: “Reduce our footprint 15% without increasing operating cost.”
deck.lead: One sentence in. A constraint search over 2,098 scenario combinations out. Real result, from the deployed instance:

table.caption: What the engine put in the plan

deck.say: Asked for 15%. It returned a plan that clears the carbon constraint and saves money — and can say why each action is in it.
deck.foot: Constraint search over a stored baseline; every scenario in the result satisfies both constraints by construction (tested).
deck.notes: Ask for the 15% out loud, then read the result out loud. The 33.8% and the $775K saving are real, from the deployed instance.

deck.title: An agent that orchestrates tools, over an engine that cannot be argued with.

left.lead: 13 tools — and the first turn is forced to call one.
left.text: The model cannot answer a quantitative question from its own head.
A pure-stdlib BM25 ranker pulls the methodology passages behind a claim, so “why is that factor defensible” is answered from a source of record.
FastAPI serves the UI and the API on a single port: no CORS layer, no second deployment, no vendor onboarding.

right.text: Next.js static export · FastAPI · SQLite · Gemini over a gateway key · i18n EN/ID with no extra dependency.
One systemd unit behind a Tailscale Funnel today; Cloud Run / Firebase is the judging-path deployment, kept to a single command.
No compliance reporting (CSRD, SB 253, CDP), no supplier portal or ERP connectors, curated point factors, linear scenario maths — stated, not discovered.

deck.notes: Do not oversell the agent. Say exactly what it does: forced first tool call, retrieval that cites, and the smoke test that fails when the key quietly stops working.

deck.title: 138 tests. A smoke test that fails on a working-looking key. One process.

bullets.text: A projection plus its saving equals the baseline. Constraint search only ever returns scenarios that satisfy the constraints. 138 tests, runnable without credentials.
A dead key produces no error — it produces a correct answer from the deterministic router while the UI still claims the model. The smoke test exists to catch exactly that.
pytest, tsc --noEmit, production build and preflight outputs are in the repository with the commands that produced them.

deck.foot: Verified 2026-10-15: backend 36s · frontend typecheck + static export ~1 min · preflight READY — agent answers by real Gemini; two honest warnings: 16 approved actions on the plan, curated-only factors (no Climatiq key).
deck.notes: This is the credibility slide: every acceptance claim in this deck maps to a command in the repo.

deck.title: From carbon accounting to carbon action.
deck.say: Watershed, Persefoni, Sweep and SINAI already do accounting, ingestion and scenario planning. We do not claim to be the first AI carbon platform. The narrower claim: their AI targets the input pipeline — ours is a contract on the output.
deck.close: Carbon reporting tells you where you are. CarbonPilot tells you what to do next.
deck.foot: Demonstration build — stated boundaries, not avoided ones.
deck.notes: Concede the category first; naming the incumbents makes the narrow claim credible. Then close on the line.

deck.title: Built for grids that make decarbonisation hard.

bullets.lead: A public facility, not a slide.
bullets.text: Twenty JAPAC grids, one documented basis, built on CC BY 4.0 open data — reusable by any team in the region.
Reach into regional mid-market teams that reporting platforms under-serve.
Wherever a model could plausibly invent a number, don’t let it. A deterministic engine with an explaining agent is the audit-grade shape for quantified AI.

deck.notes: Impact here is honest: the benchmark is open data, the product is bilingual, and the engine-over-model rule is the transferable idea.

deck.title: From CSV to the mid-market ERP.

bullets.text: AWS / GCP / Azure billing, Xero, SAP — per-account mapping on the same ingestion pipeline.

bullets.lead: Compliance modules on the same ledger.
bullets.text: CSRD, SB 253, CDP reports from the same audit trail, not a separate tool.
Climatiq is wired and config-ready; isolation is the next engineering step, not an open question.
Static export + one process today; Cloud Run / Firebase is the scale path with no architectural change.

deck.foot: The boundaries in this deck are the honest ones: no compliance reporting yet, curated factors, linear scenario maths.
deck.notes: Feasibility and scalability in one slide: the next steps are additions to a pipeline that already exists.

deck.title: From carbon accounting to carbon action.
deck.say: CarbonPilot — an AI carbon decision engine for JAPAC, built on Google AI, submitted to the AI Builder Cup 2026.
deck.foot: Prototype live · repository public at submission · proposal deck and 3-minute demo video included.
deck.notes: End on the loop and the URL. The repo goes public the moment the submission goes in.

explainer.text: CarbonPilot is an AI carbon decision engine.
Most companies can already measure their carbon. Our demo company emits eleven thousand, two hundred and eight tonnes of CO2 a year. What they cannot do is decide what to do about it.

Location matters more than most actions. The same four point three million kilowatt hours costs three thousand and thirty six tonnes on Indonesia's grid — rank nineteen of twenty, coal at sixty nine percent — and just three hundred and ninety nine tonnes in New Zealand.
CarbonPilot turns that into a decision loop: measure, diagnose, simulate, act.
One rule keeps the loop trustworthy: the language model never produces a carbon number. A deterministic engine computes every kilogram. The model chooses the analysis, and explains the result.

Ask it to cut the footprint fifteen percent without raising operating cost, and it returns a thirty three point eight percent reduction — and seven hundred and seventy five thousand dollars a year saved.
From carbon accounting to carbon action. This is CarbonPilot.

demo.text: This is CarbonPilot — an AI carbon decision engine. It is a working prototype, live, and every number you are about to see comes from the deployed instance.

The dashboard opens with the statement: eleven thousand, two hundred and eight tonnes a year, sixty one percent of it Scope 3 — procurement, travel, cloud. Cloud is just two point four percent of the carbon, but a third of the spend. That mismatch is the conversation.
Ingest maps first, calculates second. The CSV columns are mapped to canonical activities and scopes, the interpretation is previewed, and nothing is written until it has been confirmed.
Diagnose finds what actually moved. A robust outlier test flags the months that changed, and attributes each one to the activities that changed with it — with the arithmetic shown on every row.

Simulate is the core. One sentence in: reduce the footprint fifteen percent without increasing operating cost. The engine evaluates twenty one hundred scenarios and returns a plan: thirty three point eight percent reduction, three thousand seven hundred and ninety tonnes saved, and seven hundred seventy five thousand dollars a year cheaper.
Act turns it into a register. Every action is ranked on carbon, cost and effort, plotted on the matrix, and every recommendation states its trade-off — and its arithmetic.
And the JAPAC view prices the same load against twenty regional grids — so location stops being a footnote and becomes a decision. The whole product is bilingual, English and Bahasa Indonesia.
From carbon accounting to carbon action. CarbonPilot, for the Google Cloud AI Builder Cup 2026.
